text: each step reads 3.44 gb of weights (2.82 gb of layers and 0.62 gb for the output head) plus the cache: 229 kb per context token per beam, about 1.2 gb for three beams at a 1,700-token context. at the measured 79 to 91 gb/s that caps a single clip near 26 steps per second with a short context and near 20 with a long one.
19.2 to 21.7 steps per second, about 85 to 95 percent of that ceiling. three experiments in a row landed inside noise, so this is a plateau.

bound by gpu arithmetic. apple's matrix kernel measured 2.7 tflops here. a 2-minute prefill is about 5.9 tflop of work, so about 2.2 s at best, against 2.3 s now. a short prefill is about 0.24 s, of which 88 ms is widening the weights to 32-bit.
past about 12 rows the step is bound by gpu arithmetic, not memory. sharing weight reads is worth about 1.3x to 1.4x in total throughput on this mac, not the 12 to 20x the plan guessed.

same accuracy: met on the three golden clips, with at most 36 percent of the safety margin used. speed: 4.3x to 6.3x realtime, at the top of the plan's 4 to 6x estimate. throughput: 6.2x to 6.3x. latency: 0.30 s to first text on a short file. live first draft 0.7 to 1.1 s against a goal of about 0.5 s, not met.

a cheaper live draft pass. a pass costs about 60 ms to encode, 236 ms to prefill and 45 ms per new token. reuse between passes only helps phrases longer than one 8-second encoder window, so the first draft needs a different idea, such as keeping a 32-bit copy of the decoder weights (5.6 gb) to skip the 88 ms widening.
